clue.text: Beardless but impudent

definitions.meaning: having a face with no beard, literally bare of hair
shamelessly bold and unconcealed in rudeness

explanation.surface: A clean-shaven man who is nonetheless cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a face left bare of whiskers, and figuratively brazen, shameless conduct.

clue.text: Secondary highway in Norfolk

definitions.meaning: a ... is a British secondary road, written ...
the Norfolk ... are shallow lakes in that English county

explanation.surface: A minor road somewhere in rural Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain classes lesser roads as B roads; Norfolk is an English county famous for its Broads, shallow waterways.
explanation.definitionFit: A B-class road is a lesser highway, and a broad is one of the lakes of eastern England's Norfolk.

clue.text: Winding up drunk

definitions.meaning: winding line onto a reel, as an angler does
staggering unsteadily from too much alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone finishing off the evening the worse for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing line is wound in on a reel, and a tipsy person staggers or sways.

clue.text: He looks for a catch if upset by Union leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the little word if is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: General William Sherman led Union armies in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Someone seeking a marriage catch, unless a trade-union boss upsets things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' suggests a trade unionist, but it is a Civil War general of the Union side. 'upset' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is someone who tries to land fish, so he seeks a catch.

clue.text: With arms and legs well shaped and washed

parts.note: something washed has been made clean
having limbs, i.e. limbed

explanation.surface: A description of a freshly bathed, shapely physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a body with neat, well-proportioned limbs, so trim and shapely.

clue.text: Mock-up for a medicine man

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cod is a British adjective for fake or mock, as in cod Latin

explanation.surface: A model or mock-up made for a tribal healer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock-up' looks like one word for a model; it is MOCK = COD, with 'up' reversing it to DOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is informal for a physician, who practises medicine.

clue.text: Tied up on the way

definitions.meaning: fastened with rope or cord
heading towards a destination

explanation.surface: A captive trussed up while being transported.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both tethered with cords and headed for a destination.

clue.text: Brute exhorting one to piety

definitions.meaning: a savage animal or a cruel person
urging someone to be a saint, written as ... with ST the usual abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A brutal man is being urged to become devout.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE A ST: an exhortation to be a saint, ST being the standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A savage animal or cruel person is called a brute; and read as three words it urges someone towards sainthood.

clue.text: More inspired, this view of the future

definitions.meaning: inspired by Sir Thomas More, author of the book Utopia
an idealised, perfect vision of society to come

explanation.surface: A loftier, more inspiring vision of times ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like a comparative, but it is Sir Thomas More, whose 1516 book Utopia described an ideal island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic visions of a perfect society take their name from More's book.

clue.text: Fell out because underworld rests on a spirit of avarice

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece resting on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
greed is the spirit or vice of avarice

explanation.surface: A quarrel arose because hell is built on greed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out is to quarrel, i.e. be at odds or argue.

clue.text: Keep an eye on the bishop's position

definitions.meaning: supervise or watch over
a bishop is placed over his see, his diocese

explanation.surface: Watching what a bishop is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; he holds authority over it, giving OVER SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to watch and direct; and a prelate stands above his diocese.

clue.text: Window-cleaner's instant tea is outside

indicators.note: outside means the tea and the word is go round the word for instant

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: A window-cleaner drinks instant tea out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant tea' reads as a soluble drink, and 'Window-cleaner's' as a person; 'outside' wraps the tea and 'is' round the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather cloth is used to polish windows dry.

clue.text: The energy needed for an organized campaign

definitions.meaning: vigour and determination
a concerted effort

explanation.surface: Getting a well-run campaign going takes vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both personal vigour and a concerted push for a cause.

clue.text: It is not far off being a serious accident

definitions.text: It is not far off being a serious accident

parts.words: It is not far off being a serious accident
parts.note: read literally, something close at hand; the idiom is a narrow escape from disaster

explanation.surface: A description of a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is an event that very nearly became a disaster.

clue.text: Allurements of tart involved in court cases

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside court cases

parts.note: lawsuits are actions

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters of tart are jumbled

explanation.surface: A loose woman embroiled in lawsuits as an enticement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a person in the surface; 'involved' jumbles it to TTRA, and 'in' places that just after the first letter of the lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Allurements are things that draw people in: enticements.

clue.text: Power kept by the master

definitions.meaning: a logarithm, an exponent or power in mathematics
a ship's master keeps a record of the voyage

explanation.surface: A ship's captain holding authority.
explanation.walkthrough: In maths a logarithm is the power to which a base is raised; a ship's master writes up its daily record.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent in maths and a captain's voyage journal both go by this short word.

clue.text: Undiscovered reason for a now hopeless crusade

parts.note: something not yet found is lost
a cause is a reason for something

explanation.surface: An unknown motive behind a doomed campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign with no hope of success is a doomed movement.

clue.text: Keeping the alimony

definitions.meaning: upkeep, keeping things in good repair
money paid to support a former spouse

explanation.surface: Holding on to one's divorce settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep of property, and payments for an ex-spouse's support, share this word.

clue.text: Bumpy land due to subsidence

indicators.note: subsidence makes the ground shift and settle, so the letters of land due to are rearranged

explanation.surface: Uneven ground caused by the land sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subsidence' shuffles LAND DUE TO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in small knobs or lumps, hence uneven.

clue.text: Season meals for those about to dive in

definitions.text: for those about to dive in

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
board means daily meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Seasonal catering laid on for swimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers bounce off a flexible plank to launch into the pool.

clue.text: Make a thorough search for smuggled sherry

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled is ran
sack is an old name for sherry or similar white wine

explanation.surface: Customs officers combing a ship for contraband sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to go through a place hunting for something.

clue.text: You and I would be one

definitions.meaning: we would, contracted with an apostrophe
become joined as one in marriage

explanation.surface: A proposal: together we would make a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraction of we would, and to marry, two people joined in matrimony.

clue.text: Justify jingoism

definitions.meaning: give grounds for something
a jingoist's ..., an aggressive patriotic tirade

explanation.surface: Defending warlike patriotism.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as WAR RANT: jingoism is aggressive patriotism that clamours for war.
explanation.definitionFit: To give grounds for something; and split in two, a tirade urging armed conflict.

clue.text: Can doctor be reinstated by agreement?

indicators.note: the letters of can doctor are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a struck-off doctor could get his job back by a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be reinstated' rearranges CAN DOCTOR; 'doctor' itself looks like the anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal pact, especially between a church and a state.

clue.text: Command sequence

definitions.meaning: an instruction to be obeyed
arrangement one after another

explanation.surface: An instruction followed by a list.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction to obey, and an arrangement in series, share this word.

clue.text: No place for commoner members?

parts.note: the upper chamber of the British parliament seats peers, not commoners

explanation.surface: A club too exclusive for ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK parliament, whose members are peers rather than commoners.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamber of peers is where commoners do not sit.

clue.text: Weekend news chief more than satisfied

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, part of the weekend
ed is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss enjoying a satisfying weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutted beyond merely full, so having had more than enough.

clue.text: Internationally supported to become independent

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is the international body
helped or assisted, i.e. aided

explanation.surface: A country helped by the world community towards independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Internationally supported' reads as one idea about foreign aid, yet the definition is its opposite, 'independent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting alone without help means being self-reliant.

clue.text: Old tallow candle means lower lights

definitions.meaning: a candle made by dipping a wick in tallow
to ... headlights is to angle them down

explanation.surface: An antique candle provides dimmer illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle made by plunging a wick in fat, and lowering a car's headlamp beams.

clue.text: Survive all but the final ball of the innings

definitions.meaning: live longer than, endure beyond

definitions.text: all but the final ball of the innings
definitions.meaning: in cricket a batting side all out on the last ball

explanation.surface: Lasting through almost the whole of a cricket innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings ends when the side is all out; here the dismissal comes at the very end, OUT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive someone is to endure longer; and the cricket reading puts the dismissal at the close.

clue.text: Rakes specially designed for river gravel

indicators.note: something specially designed is made anew, so the letters of rakes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Garden rakes made for raking gravel by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eskar (usually esker) is a ridge of gravel laid down by a stream under a glacier.

clue.text: Job appointment offered at some future time

parts.note: a post is a job
to have dated someone is to have offered an appointment, a date

explanation.surface: A job interview set for a later day.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque marked with a later date takes effect at a future time.
